vintages.fy_capex_note: $90 billion to $95 billion in CapEx for FY2027, with not more than $70 billion in net cash CapEx (p4)

multi_year_targets.note: No new multi-year figures; FY2027 revenue guidance raised to at least $90 billion (+34%) and non-GAAP EPS to $8.10 (p7). New Q1 RPO (mostly Pre-Pay/BYOH) will not affect CapEx or revenues until FY2028 or beyond (p3). Gross margin expected to flatten over the next couple of years after the ramp (p14). New Mexico and Wisconsin sites: no impact on previously stated FY2027 revenue or earnings guidance (p10). More detail promised at Investor Day in October (p8, p14).

vintages._note: Verbatim from 'Guidance for Q1 FY 2027': 'Total Revenues are expected to grow from 27% to 29% in both constant currency and USD. Total Cloud revenue is expected to grow between 57% and 63% in constant currency and...58% and 64% in USD. Non-GAAP earnings per share is expected to grow between 16% and 19% and be between $1.71 and $1.75 in constant currency and grow between 17% and 20% and be between $1.72 and $1.76 in USD.' Under 'Guidance for Full FY 2027' (this is the release that first sets FY2027 guidance): 'we confirm our prior revenue guidance of $90 billion total revenue and raise our non-GAAP EPS guidance to $8.05, which is growth of 18% after adjusting for the one-time events of selling our Ampere chip business and Bloom Energy warrants in fiscal year 2026.' Per Footnote 1, that 18% growth figure is measured against an adjusted FY2026 non-GAAP EPS base of $6.83 (i.e. FY2026's reported $7.63 excluding the Ampere/Bloom Energy one-time gains), not against the $7.63 reported figure -- important for like-for-like FY2027 EPS growth modeling.
vintages.fy_capex_note: FY2027 net cash outlay for capital expenditures of around $70 billion; customer prepayments and timing impacts of around $20-25 billion mean reported CapEx will be higher by that amount (p8)

multi_year_targets.note: Long-term outlook from Analyst Day reconfirmed: 'plus 31% revenue CAGR and plus 28% EPS CAGR through our fiscal year 2030' (p8); 'full reconfirmation from my side on the long-term targets' (p10). Project-level ROIC 'in the high 20s at a steady state' (p10). Revenues and earnings expected to accelerate in 2H FY2027 (p8). Next Investor Day October 28 in Las Vegas (p8).

vintages._note: Verbatim from 'Guidance for Q4 FY26': 'Total revenues are expected to grow from 18% to 20% in constant currency [total_revenue_growth_pct field above uses the USD range of 19%-21%; CC range was 18%-20%] and are expected to grow from 19% to 21% in USD. Total Cloud revenue is expected to grow between 44% to 48% in constant currency and...46% to 50% in USD. Non-GAAP earnings per share is expected to grow between 15% to 17% and be between $1.92 and $1.96 in constant currency and...between $1.96 and $2.00 in USD.' Separately, under 'Guidance for Fiscal Years 2026 and 2027': 'For fiscal year 2026, we expect revenue of $67 billion and capital expenditures of $50 billion. This is unchanged from our most recent previous guidance' (fy_total_revenue_at_least = 67000 reflects this FY2026 revenue guidance; FY2026 capex guidance of $50,000M has no dedicated schema field). The release also states 'For fiscal year 2027, we are raising total revenue guidance to $90 billion' -- a preliminary FY2027 revenue figure disclosed here, ahead of the formal initial FY2027 guidance (including EPS) set in the Q4 FY2026 release.

No quantified forward guidance (next-quarter or full-year) and no qualitative outlook commentary of the kind seen in Q1 is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. Management commentary in this release focused on the Ampere divestiture, chip neutrality strategy, datacenter buildout, and AI product strategy, not on forward financial guidance.

vintages._note: No quantified next-quarter (Q1 FY2026) guidance table is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. Initial FY2026 full-year outlook IS given, but only qualitatively (as direct CEO quotes), not as specific $ revenue or EPS figures: CEO Safra Catz stated Oracle expects 'total cloud growth rate -- applications plus infrastructure -- will increase from 24% in FY25 to over 40% in FY26,' 'Cloud Infrastructure growth rate is expected to increase from 50% in FY25 to over 70% in FY26,' and 'RPO is likely to grow more than 100% in FY26.' Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison added that MultiCloud database revenue grew 115% quarter-over-quarter and that 'triple-digit MultiCloud revenue growth' is expected to continue in FY26, and that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure consumption revenue 'grew 62% in Q4' with growth expected to accelerate further in FY26. These are the only FY2026 guidance-related statements in the exhibit; fy_total_revenue_at_least and fy_non_gaap_eps were not quantified and are left null per instructions rather than estimated.

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. The CEO commented qualitatively that the ~$130 billion RPO backlog 'will help drive a 15% increase in Oracle's overall revenue in our next fiscal year beginning this June' (i.e. FY2026, not a specific quarter), but no quantified next-quarter revenue growth %, cloud growth %, or non-GAAP EPS range was disclosed in the exhibit itself. Also announced: dividend increased 25% from $0.40 to $0.50/share.

Initial FY2025 full-year outlook IS given, but only qualitatively (as direct CEO quotes), not as specific $ revenue or EPS figures: CEO Safra Catz stated 'Throughout fiscal year 2025, I expect continued strong AI demand to push Oracle sales and RPO even higher -- and result in double-digit revenue growth this fiscal year. I also expect that each successive quarter should grow faster than the previous quarter -- as OCI capacity begins to catch up with demand.' Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison stated 11 of the 23 OCI datacenters being built inside Azure went live in Q4, that Oracle signed an agreement with Google to interconnect clouds and initially build 12 OCI datacenters inside Google Cloud, and that 'We expect the Oracle database to be available within the Google Cloud in September this year.' These are the only FY2025 guidance-related statements in the exhibit; fy_total_revenue_at_least and fy_non_gaap_eps were not quantified and are left null per instructions rather than estimated.

vintages._note: No quantified next-quarter (Q1 FY2024) or full-year FY2024 guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. Forward-looking commentary is qualitative only: CEO Safra Catz said FY2023 annual revenue growth 'was led by our cloud applications and infrastructure businesses which grew at a combined rate of 50% in constant currency,' that infrastructure growth was 'accelerating—with 63% growth for the full year, and 77% growth in the fourth quarter,' and that 'both of our two strategic cloud businesses are getting bigger—and growing faster. That bodes well for another strong year in FY24.' Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison said that LLM developers 'plus 30 other AI development companies have recently signed contracts to purchase more than $2 billion of capacity in Oracle's Gen2 Cloud.' The exhibit states that without the USD strengthening, Q4 non-GAAP EPS 'would have been $0.03 higher.' fy_total_revenue_at_least and fy_non_gaap_eps were not quantified and are left null rather than estimated.

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. The only guidance reference is retrospective: CEO Safra Catz said 'Oracle's non-GAAP earnings per share growth hit the high end of our guidance—up 13% in constant currency to $1.22,' that 'Oracle's cloud businesses now exceed $16 billion in annualized revenue,' and that the Gen2 infrastructure business was 'up 65% in Q3 in constant currency.' Forward-looking commentary is qualitative only: Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison said 'we expect the signing of new healthcare contracts to accelerate over the next few quarters.' Also announced: quarterly dividend increased 25% from $0.32 to $0.40 per share (Ellison did not participate in the deliberation or vote). The exhibit states that without the USD strengthening, Q3 non-GAAP EPS 'would have been 5 cents higher.'

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. The only guidance reference is retrospective: CEO Safra Catz said 'In Q2, Oracle's total revenue grew 25% in constant currency—exceeding the high end of our guidance by more than $200 million,' noting infrastructure and applications cloud grew 59% and 45% in constant currency, Fusion Cloud ERP 28% and NetSuite Cloud ERP 29%. Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison's commentary on the healthcare mission ('we are just beginning our mission to modernize healthcare information systems') is qualitative. The exhibit also states that without the USD strengthening, Q2 non-GAAP EPS 'would have been 9 cents higher.'

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release; Oracle communicates quarterly guidance verbally on its earnings conference call, which is a separate document not part of this 8-K exhibit. Qualitative commentary in the exhibit: CEO Safra Catz said Q1 total revenue grew 23% in constant currency 'beating guidance by $200 million'; that 'Even without Cerner, our total revenue grew 8% in constant currency'; that 'As our cloud businesses become a larger-and-larger percentage of our overall business, we expect our constant currency organic revenue growth rate to hit double-digits with a corresponding increase in earnings per share'; and that 'Cerner will also positively impact revenue and earnings per share growth in the coming quarters as we fully integrate Cerner into Oracle.' The exhibit also states that without the USD strengthening, Q1 GAAP and non-GAAP EPS 'would have been 8 cents higher.'

No quantified next-quarter (Q1 FY2023) or FY2023 guidance table is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. Qualitative outlook only: CEO Safra Catz stated that the Q4 infrastructure cloud growth of 39% in constant currency 'indicates that our infrastructure business has now entered a hyper-growth phase' and that, coupled with 'the newly acquired Cerner applications business', 'Oracle finds itself in position to deliver stellar revenue growth over the next several quarters'. No revenue growth %, cloud growth %, or EPS figures were given in the exhibit; all quantified fields are left null rather than estimated.

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. Qualitative commentary only: CEO Safra Catz stated that Q3's 7% constant-currency revenue growth was 'our highest quarterly organic revenue growth rate since we began our transition to the cloud' and that 'Total Cloud revenue which includes Cloud Infrastructure and Cloud Applications is now over $11 billion a year'; management also said it remains 'confident that our investments in [Oxford Nanopore and Ampere] will deliver very strong returns for Oracle'. Chairman/CTO Larry Ellison said MySQL HeatWave would be available on AWS and Microsoft Azure 'in a few weeks'.

No quantified forward guidance is contained in this Exhibit 99.1 press release. The only forward-looking commentary is qualitative: CEO Safra Catz said the infrastructure and applications cloud businesses (growing 22%) 'are approaching $11 billion in annualized revenue' and that the Gen2 infrastructure businesses 'are growing even faster - and accelerating'; backward-looking remarks note Q2 non-GAAP EPS beat guidance by $0.10 and constant-currency revenue beat guidance by $200 million. Also announced: the board increased the share repurchase authorization by $10 billion.
